metadata.case_name: TANG CHI WA v. DR ALBERT Y.H. CHAN

plaintiff.occupation_before: Surveyor (employed by Hyundai Engineering & Construction Limited)
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: Less physically demanding work in an office or as a sales assistant, store keeper, caretaker
plaintiff.education_level: Educated in China up to Form 3

injuries.description: Right sciatic nerve damage causing foot drop / right sciatic nerve palsy
source: it caused damage to his right sciatic nerve which in turn caused "foot drop", a condition which will now be permanent.
The diagnosis was right "foot drop" and right sciatic nerve palsy.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of sciatic nerve at hip or thigh level

injuries.description: Injury to left shoulder and neck sustained at work on 3 October 2000
source: the plaintiff who had been suffering from the effects of an injury to his left shoulder and neck which he had sustained at work on 3 October 2000,
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the shoulder or upper arm, unspecified

manifestations.description: Weakness and numbness of the lower part of his right leg
Requires wearing a foot brace / splint to prevent foot drop
Can no longer run or play sports at the pre-accident level
Slight abnormality of gait detected on walking

treatments_received: Outpatient follow-up (O & T Department, Caritas Medical Centre)
Follow-up at Prosthetic & Orthotic Department (Caritas Medical Centre)
Consultation with orthopaedic surgeon (Mr Michael Lau FRCS)
Bonesetter treatment (in Hong Kong and China)
Medical treatment at different hospitals/clinics in China
Consultation with Dr Kwok Che Cheung

losses.description: Permanent need to wear a foot brace and diminished mobility with an abnormal gait

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Activities such as dancing at discotheques, country walks, jogging and playing basketball have been very seriously curtailed
Active social life curtailed (e.g. discotheque dancing) and feelings of inhibition about wearing shorts because of the brace
